reading.limits: historical comparators for both C1 and C2; exchangeability assumed, not designed; thresholds are operational; fresh seeds: a population-rate replication of 0.7.0's record, not a repeat of its seeds
reading.meaning: the fresh-seed replication (variant F) does not sustain the original low-empty result under the specified rules. This does not necessarily mean that no advantage over 0.9.1 remains: p2 can indicate deterioration relative to the old 0.7.0 record while some advantage over 0.9.1 persists (see C1 beside it).
reading.next_step_prespecified: reassess whether the original 4-versus-16 contrast remains an appropriate optimization target; verified correctness fixes keep their value.
reading.test_assumptions: Both tests are exact sign-flip tests: 'exact' refers to the calculation of the p-value (full enumeration of the sign patterns), given the assumptions. The assumptions are that, under the null, each question's pair of per-question empty counts (rep, historical record) is exchangeable, i.e. the historical comparator behaves as a draw from the same process as the new run on that question, and that questions are the independent units. Neither is designed: the comparators are historical records, so time, state and other changes since are confounded with the comparison.
reading.text: movement toward the newer engine's count: the original gap is reported as not reproduced, without claiming equivalence; no expensive bisection without a reproducible target (amendment 12)
